summary: The morning after the late meeting: The morning after a late night meeting, {household member} asks where the player was and what it cost the house.
realLife: One life: A Missouri legislator's wife says his job often takes him from home, she has adjusted her work to be a solo parent, and the children miss their father at school events and sports. She says it is worth the sacrifice. Another: A Winston-Salem council member whose job takes him from dinner time and sports pickups. He talked it over with his wife and children first, uses paid time off for council duties, and the household uses shared schedules and group chats. Another: A Utah congressman spent four days a week in Washington while his wife raised the children alone in the week; he sets aside regular family time. A former Santa Clara mayor moved her daughters to another school after a backlash over her vote. Another: Michigan governors and officials said they felt guilt about time lost with their children; one governor regretted sending his children to boarding school; the current First Family tries to eat Sunday dinners together. Another: A Salt Lake County councilwoman who took only boards that met during school hours, cut her income by half and protected date nights and tech-free family time. Her husband took on more of the house and his employer gave him less travel.
